name: Self-Relevance Effect
description: Information tied to the self is remembered better than otherwise similar information processed in less self-related ways. Asking people to connect material to their own goals, identity, or circumstances often makes it stick.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to personalization, profile/setup flows, self-tracking, goal setting, reflective prompts, and educational products that ask users to map information onto their own situation rather than just passively read it.
prevalence_note: Relevant to personalization and reflective-product design, but not usually taught as a mainstream named law in everyday general UX practice.

findings.description: A meta-analysis of the self-reference literature found that information encoded in relation to the self is remembered better than information encoded in less self-related ways, directly backing the canonical self-reference/self-relevance memory advantage.
findings.source_title: The self-reference effect in memory: A meta-analysis.
